sources.title: The Xi'an Drum Tower: Echoes of the Past, Still Heard Today
sources.content:
Xi'an Drum Tower: Complete Text Content

Overview & History
The Xi'an Drum Tower stands 200 meters northwest of the Bell Tower. "Built in 1380 during Emperor Zhu Yuanzhang's reign, this ancient edifice predates the Bell Tower by four years, marking it as one of the oldest and best-preserved drum towers in China."

Purpose & Function
The structure served as the city's official timekeeper. "The original giant drum was struck daily to signal time, earning the tower its iconic name." It functioned as a chronological device for ancient Xi'an residents.

Architecture & Design
The tower displays impressive dimensions and imperial craftsmanship. Standing "34 meters high," it rests on "a massive rectangular base" measuring "52.6-meter length and 38-meter width." The architectural style features "a two-story wooden structure" topped with "a double-eaved, hip-style roof," reserved for China's most prestigious buildings.

Decorative elements include "intricate architectural paintings" reflecting imperial hierarchy, along with "powdered gold dragons and twining patterns" throughout its interior.

Cultural Inscriptions
Two significant plaques beneath the third eave display important phrases: "Land of Civil and Martial Arts" and "Heard in Heaven," symbolizing wisdom, strength, and divine connection to governance.

Modern Restoration
In 1996, the tower received major restoration work. A new drum was installed, measuring "1.8 meters tall" with "a 2.83-meter diameter," crafted from high-quality cowhide, designed to welcome the 21st century.

Visitor Information
Ticket Prices:
Individual: 30 RMB
Combined Bell and Drum Tower: 50 RMB
Free entry for children and seniors over 65
Half-price for students with valid ID

Hours: 08:30-18:00 (last entry 17:30)

Transportation:
Subway: Line 2 to Bell Tower Station, Exit C (2-minute walk)
Bus: Routes 7, 8, 601, 611, 618

Performances: Second-floor exhibition hall hosts drum and bell music at 9:30, 10:15, 11:00, 11:45, 14:00, 15:00, 16:00, 17:00 (seasonal variations possible)

Visitor Experience
First Floor: After ticket inspection, visitors encounter "a circle of historically arranged drums" with views of the distant Bell Tower, ideal for photography.
Second Floor: Displays ancient artifacts and provides expansive cityscape views. Hourly musical performances occur on the first floor.
Summit: Reaching the top reveals "a breathtaking panoramic view of Xi'an." The perspective showcases "a harmonious blend of ancient architecture and modern advancements."

Nighttime Atmosphere
After sunset, "the Drum Tower transforms into a radiant beacon, glowing beautifully against the dark sky." Golden illumination highlights architectural details, creating photogenic opportunities.

Optimal Visit Times
Early morning visits provide peaceful exploration before crowds. Late afternoon visits capture "golden hour glow" as sunlight bathes the structure warmly.

Nearby Attractions
Xi'an Bell Tower: Historical landmark featuring grand architecture and ancient bells with city views
Muslim Quarter: Vibrant cultural district with street food, traditional markets, and local delicacies
Great Mosque of Xi'an: Islamic-Chinese architectural blend offering peaceful exploration

sources.title: Drum Tower - Xi'an Travel Guide
sources.content:
Xi'an Drum Tower - Complete Information

Location & Setting
The Drum Tower stands adjacent to Xi'an's Bell Tower and overlooks the gray-tiled roofs of the nearby Muslim Quarter.

Historical Background
"First built in 1380, with restorations in 1669, 1739, and 1853," the structure reaches 33 meters in height. During the Ming Dynasty, Chinese cities used bell and drum towers "to help keep time and transmit news."

Architecture & Features
The tower has a rectangular shape, distinguishing it from its circular Bell Tower neighbor. A parapet surrounds the second story. The restored second floor now functions as an antique shop and hosts art exhibitions. It displays "a collection of a variety of drums in different shapes and sizes and made from different materials." Ming and Qing dynasty furniture occupies the third floor.

Visitor Experience
The structure appears particularly striking when "illuminated with colorful lights" in the evening. Drum performances occur "several times during the morning and the afternoon."

Practical Details
Hours: 8:30am-6pm
Admission: 35 CNY (tower only); 50 CNY (Bell Tower/Drum Tower combo)
Duration: Approximately 30 minutes

Visitors should contact their travel agent for current performance schedules.

sources.title: Xian Drum Tower: Opening Hours, Ticket, Fee, Performance, Map
sources.content:
Xi'an Drum Tower - ChinaDiscovery

The Drum Tower is a timber-brick tower built in 1380 during the Ming dynasty and is now used as a museum displaying collections of various drums and cultural relics. It is about 34 meters (112 feet) high and 53 meters long (172 feet), covering an area of 1998.8 square meters, with two floors, mainly in red and yellow.

Opening Hours: 8:30am-20:30pm (April 1st to October 10th) / 8:30am-18:00pm (October 11th to March 31th).

Tickets for the Drum Tower are quite affordable, usually around 35 RMB. If you're planning to visit the nearby Bell Tower too, look for combo tickets that cover both landmarks at a discount.

Address: To the West of Bell Tower, at West Street, Lianhu District, Xian City. You can get here by metro—just take Line 2 or 4 and get off at Bell and Drum Tower Station.

There are 24 drums in the north and south sides of the tower with traditional Chinese characters written on it, which are 24 solar terms of Chinese lunar calendar and used to guide the agricultural production and symbolizes good fortune for the coming years.

For the best experience, plan your visit either early in the morning to beat the crowds or in the evening when the Drum Tower lights up with beautiful illumination. From the upper levels, you'll enjoy great views overlooking the bustling Xi'an Muslim Quarter and the busy city streets below.

sources.title: Drum Tower Xi'an Travel Guide Tickets Hours and Tips
sources.content:
Drum Tower Xi'an Travel Guide

The Xi'an Drum Tower, built in 1380 during the Ming Dynasty, is one of the most iconic historical landmarks in Xi'an. Standing at a height of 34 meters and covering an area of nearly 2,000 square meters, the Drum Tower is an impressive display of traditional Chinese architecture.

The tower originally housed a large drum used to mark the hours and announce important events to the city's residents. Today, it serves as a museum and cultural site.

Tickets: Individual ticket 30 RMB, combo with Bell Tower 50 RMB.
Hours: April-October 8:30-21:30; November-March 8:30-18:00.

Performances of traditional drum music are held multiple times daily, typically at 9:30, 10:15, 11:00, 11:45, 14:00, 15:00, 16:00, and 17:00.

The Drum Tower is located at the entrance to the Muslim Quarter, making it easy to combine a visit with food exploration.

sources.title: Essential Travel Tips for Xi'an Drum Tower & Bell Tower
sources.content:
Essential Travel Tips for Xi'an Drum Tower & Bell Tower

The Bell Tower and Drum Tower are two iconic Ming Dynasty landmarks located in the heart of Xi'an. The Bell Tower was built in 1384, and the Drum Tower was built in 1380.

The two towers are just 200 meters apart and can easily be visited together. A combo ticket covering both costs 50 CNY, saving 10 CNY compared to buying separate tickets.

Both towers offer panoramic views of Xi'an's city center, including the busy streets and the nearby Muslim Quarter.

Performances of traditional music, including ancient chime bells at the Bell Tower and drum performances at the Drum Tower, are held multiple times daily.

Best times to visit: Early morning for fewer crowds, or evening for stunning illuminated views of both towers.

sources.title: 西安鼓楼_百度百科
sources.content:
西安鼓楼 - 完整信息总结

基本信息
西安鼓楼位于陕西省西安市中心北院门街南端，西大街北侧，距西安钟楼约200米。建于明洪武十三年（1380年），比钟楼早建4年。

历史沿革
该建筑由长兴侯耿炳文和西安知府王宗周主持修建。清康熙三十八年（1699年）和乾隆四年（1740年）曾进行过两次重修。据记载，乾隆五年重修时，陕西小麦丰收，长安县令王瑞具体负责修缮事宜。

建筑特色
规模：占地面积1998.8平方米，总高36米，为砖木结构
形式：歇山顶重檐三滴水木构建筑，分上下两层，正面七间，进深三间
基座：长方形，全用青砖砌筑，高7.7米，东西长52.6米，南北宽38米
工艺：全楼无一铁钉，采用斗拱构造原理
彩绘：使用和玺彩绘和旋子彩绘，绘有沥粉金龙

文物遗存
牌匾：南面"文武盛地"，北面"声闻于天"，均为蓝底金字木匾，长8米，宽3.6米。文革期间被毁，2005年4月29日重新悬挂。
字画：1954年取回齐白石创作的10幅画作、一副对联，以及李可染与陈半丁的画作。
鼓楼大鼓：1996年重制，高1.8米，鼓面直径2.83米，上有泡钉1996个。

文化活动
中国鼓文化展：陈列各式鼓类，包括陶鼓、鼍鼓、石鼓、铜鼓等数十种
"晨钟暮鼓"仿古表演：每日定时鸣钟鸣鼓
鼓乐编钟表演

历史与艺术价值
西安鼓楼是中国现存明代建筑中仅次于故宫太和殿、长陵棱恩殿的大体量古代建筑，在同类建筑中年代最久、保存最完好，具有重要的历史、艺术和科学价值。

保护地位
1956年8月6日：陕西省重点文物保护单位
1996年11月20日：全国重点文物保护单位
2007年：列入中国十大名楼

旅游信息
门票：30元/人次，钟鼓楼套票50元
开放时间：2月12日-10月10日08:30-21:30；12月24日-次年2月11日08:30-18:00
交通：地铁2号线钟楼站下车

sources.title: 西安鼓楼游玩攻略 - 携程攻略
sources.content:
西安鼓楼游玩攻略

基本介绍
西安鼓楼与钟楼相望，是古城的标志性建筑之一。鼓楼始建于明洪武十三年（1380年），登上鼓楼，能够看到一面高1.8米的大鼓，还有24面刻着24节气的红鼓。此鼓楼内还展览着明清家具、瓷器和齐白石的书画。

门票价格
成人票：30元；学生票：15元；65周岁（含）以上老人/幼童/残疾人/现役军人：免费
购票提示：可以购买钟鼓楼套票，比单买便宜10元，即套票为50元。

开放时间
旺季开放时间：1月1日至10月10日 8:30-21:30（21:00停止入场）
淡季开放时间：10月11日至12月31日 8:30-18:00（17:30停止入场）

游玩体验
游玩鼓楼时，还可以欣赏到仿古的"晨钟暮鼓"的表演，此外还有传统民乐和舞蹈的演出，每天日间6场。

交通方式
乘坐3、6路等公交在"鼓楼"站下车。或乘坐地铁2号线在"钟楼"站下车再步行5分钟即到。

咨询电话：029-87278797（鼓楼）

sources.title: Drum Tower in Xi'an - Information and guide
sources.content:
Drum Tower in Xi'an - Information and Guide

The Drum Tower was built in 1380 during the Ming Dynasty and is one of the best-preserved drum towers in China. It stands 34 meters tall on a rectangular base, with a distinctive double-eaved hip roof.

The tower houses a collection of drums including the 24 festival drums representing the 24 solar terms of the Chinese calendar. The original massive drum was used to mark the evening hours, complementing the Bell Tower's morning timekeeping.

Inside, visitors can see exhibitions of Chinese drum culture, Ming and Qing dynasty antiques, and artworks including pieces by Qi Baishi.

The Drum Tower sits at the entrance to the famous Muslim Quarter, making it an ideal starting point for exploring Xi'an's food culture.

Ticket: 30 RMB individual, 50 RMB combo with Bell Tower.
Best time: Evening for illuminated views, or morning for peaceful exploration.
